Time-varying discrete Kalman filter and smoother

Source: R/estimation.R
ctrl_kalman_filter.Rd

Run the Kalman filter on measured data for \(x_{k+1} = A x_k + B u_k + G w_k\), \(y_k = C x_k + D u_k + v_k\).

Usage

ctrl_kalman_filter(sys, y, u = NULL, Qn, Rn, x0 = NULL, P0 = NULL, G = NULL)

ctrl_kalman_smoother(filter)

Arguments

sys

A discrete time ctrl_ss model.

y

Measurements, a matrix with one row per sample (T x p).

u

Inputs (T x m), or NULL for zero input.

Qn, Rn

Process and measurement noise covariances.

x0, P0

Prior mean and covariance at the first sample (defaults: zero and the identity).

G

Process noise input matrix (default identity).

filter

A ctrl_kalman_filter result.

Value

ctrl_kalman_filter() returns an object of class ctrl_kalman_filter with filtered (T x n), predicted (T x n, row k is \(\hat x_{k|k-1}\)), P_filtered and P_predicted (n x n x T arrays), innovations, innovation_cov (p x p x T), gain (n x p x T), nis (normalized innovation squared) and loglik (Gaussian log-likelihood of the measurements). ctrl_kalman_smoother() returns a list with smoothed and P_smoothed.

Details

Conventions. x0 and P0 are the prior mean and covariance of the state at the first sample, \(\hat x_{1|0}\) and \(P_{1|0}\). Each step first updates with \(y_k\) and then predicts to \(k + 1\): $$e_k = y_k - C \hat x_{k|k-1} - D u_k, \quad S_k = C P_{k|k-1} C^\top + R_n, \quad K_k = P_{k|k-1} C^\top S_k^{-1},$$ $$\hat x_{k|k} = \hat x_{k|k-1} + K_k e_k, \quad \hat x_{k+1|k} = A \hat x_{k|k} + B u_k.$$ The covariance update uses the Joseph form \(P_{k|k} = (I - K_k C) P_{k|k-1} (I - K_k C)^\top + K_k R_n K_k^\top\), which keeps it symmetric positive semidefinite in floating point. Rows of y containing NA are treated as missing measurements (the update is skipped).

ctrl_kalman_smoother() applies the Rauch-Tung-Striebel backward pass to the filter output.

Examples

set.seed(1)
sys <- ctrl_ss(matrix(c(1, 0.1, 0, 1), 2, byrow = TRUE), c(0.005, 0.1),
               c(1, 0), dt = 0.1)
x <- c(0, 1)
y <- numeric(50)
for (k in 1:50) {
  y[k] <- x[1] + rnorm(1, sd = 0.1)
  x <- drop(sys$A %*% x) + rnorm(2, sd = c(0.001, 0.01))
}
kf <- ctrl_kalman_filter(sys, y, Qn = diag(c(1e-6, 1e-4)), Rn = 0.01)
tail(kf$filtered, 3)
#>             x1        x2
#> [48,] 4.680705 0.9807787
#> [49,] 4.764152 0.9704786
#> [50,] 4.863031 0.9717680
sm <- ctrl_kalman_smoother(kf)
